item.aggregated_output:
# Analyst evidence package

This directory contains flat JSONL sample tuples for 338 same-task bad/good
AgentReward pairs drawn from 440 source trajectories. The semantic stack is
`task -> subtask -> strategy -> action -> object -> result`.

Each line in `samples.jsonl` has exactly these fields:

- `sample_type`: pprof sample type;
- `unit`: pprof sample unit;
- `value`: signed sample value, with positive for the bad side and negative
  for the good side;
- `stack_frames`: ordered pprof frame names in leaf-to-root order; and
- `labels`: the exact pprof string labels, represented as key-to-value-list.

The file preserves duplicate tuples and source order. It contains no derived
rates, pair manifest, aggregate result summary, or rendered figure.

Basic inspection examples:

```bash
head -n 1 samples.jsonl | jq .
jq -c 'select(.value > 0)' samples.jsonl
jq -c 'select(.value < 0)' samples.jsonl
```

item.text: {"diagnosis":"Candidate/bad runs overrepresent actions whose result is explicitly marked repeated, indicating persistence with non-progressing behavior.","expected_mechanism":"Detecting repeated outcomes and forcing reassessment should reduce unproductive loops and encourage alternative actions. Cost: extra state tracking and occasional unnecessary replanning when repetition is intentional.","policy_text":"Track recent action outcomes. When an action produces the same non-progress result twice, stop repeating it, reassess the current state and objective, then choose a materially different action or explicitly terminate if no justified alternative remains.","quantitative_evidence":[{"command":"jq -r '[(if .value>0 then \"candidate/bad\" else \"base/good\" end),.stack_frames[0],(.value|if .<0 then -. else . end)]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\\t' '{all[$1]+=$3;if($2==\"result:repeated\")rep[$1]+=$3} END{for(k in all)printf \"%s repeated=%d total=%d share=%.2f%%\\n\",k,rep[k],all[k],100*rep[k]/all[k]}' | sort","finding":"Candidate/bad: 1,485 of 7,366 operations were repeated (20.16%); base/good: 224 of 3,780 (5.93%). The candidate/bad repeated-operation share was 3.40× higher, with a signed excess of 1,261 operations."},{"command":"jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]==\"result:repeated\") | [(if .value>0 then \"candidate/bad\" else \"base/good\" end),.labels.source_session[0]]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | sort -u | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c","finding":"Repeated outcomes occurred in 88 distinct candidate/bad source sessions versus 20 distinct base/good source sessions, showing recurrence beyond a single trajectory."}]}
